title: Link metadata is advanced before the document update is durably saved
reasoning: refreshLinks updates each link row's lastValue and lastSourceCommitId inside the loop before writeFileSync and commitPath run. If the write fails, or if commitPath later cannot parse/version the rewritten document, the database says the link has pulled the latest source while the document still contains the old value or has no recorded version. Future refreshes compare against the already-updated lastValue and can skip the missing update permanently.
reproduction: Make a linked target document unwritable or cause writeFileSync to fail, then call refreshLinks after the source value changes. The call throws after updateLinkValue, leaving listLinks reporting the new value/source commit even though the file was not updated.
recommendation: Apply the document write and version commit first, then update link rows only after success. Prefer wrapping link-row updates in a store transaction tied to the successful commit; on write/commit failure, leave links stale so a later refresh retries.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The smoke coverage only verifies the successful propagation path and stale=false after a successful write; it does not inject write or commit failures.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a service test that changes a source value, forces the linked document write to fail, calls refreshLinks, and asserts lastValue/lastSourceCommitId remain unchanged and stale remains true.
minimumFixScope: DocumentService.refreshLinks ordering and transaction/error handling around updateLinkValue.
